svg.title: Crank, car axle, and pulley as simple machines
svg.desc: (a) A crank with a long input radius r_i and a short but nonzero output shaft radius r_o. Both delivered forces are tangential and drive clockwise rotation; F_o is the force on the driven shaft. (b) A small axle drives a larger wheel: F_i is tangential at the top of the axle and F_o is the leftward force delivered to the road at the bottom of the wheel. Both radii are perpendicular to their forces. (c) A single fixed pulley carries one continuous rope over its upper rim, with the input pulled down on the left and a connected load supported on the right. Equal lever arms give F_i = F_o = T and MA = 1. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Crank mechanical advantage trades force for distance
Ideal rigid wheel and axle, balanced torques: Fᵢrᵢ = Fₒrₒ.
